newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Mid-Atlantic spot power eases on nuclear news.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Mid-Atlantic spot power eases on nuclear news.

text.p: Physical electricity prices in the U.S. Mid-Atlantic region erased Wednesday's gains on Thursday as the market anticipated the restoration of some nuclear power, industry sources said.
In the Pennsylvania-New Jersey-Maryland (PJM) Interconnect pool, next-day firm electricity prices for peak deliveries were quoted early at $23.00 per megawatt hour (MWh).

However, as news surfaced that PECO Energy's 1,100 megawatt Peach Bottom nuclear unit 2 would be back on line later today, prices began to fall to as low as $21.00. The bulk of business was in the $22.50 area, down from Wednesday's levels as high as $27.00.

PECO's unit in Delta, Pa., was reduced to about 15 to 20 percent power early Wednesday so that the utility could work on the turbine. Uncertainty surrounding the unit's restart resulted in reluctance on the part of some traders to close transactions.
Next week's peak prices for firm electricity were discussed in the $20.00-21.00 area, while for the remainder of October prices were flat in the $21.00-22.50 range.
November PJM prices showed some softness in the $22.45-22.75 range, as compared to Wednesday's $22.50-22.75 market.
December PJM prices held steady in the $26.50-26.85 range.
For the balance of the fourth quarter, traders reported closing deals in the $22.50-22.70 area.
Firm deliveries of peak PJM power in January and February of 1997 sold in the $30.25-30.40 range, as compared to the $30.60 offers seen on Wednesday.
Forecasters are calling for temperatures to dip to about six to 12 degrees Fahrenheit below-normal on Friday in the Northeast but then rise to only slightly below-normal this weekend.
Natgas sources said spot prices at New York city-gate for Friday delivery were mostly stronger in the $2.65-2.73 range.
